Trying to harness memetics and anomalous properties for use in the Foundation is a tricky, if not tempting possibility that often only ends with unsuccess. item.content:encoded:
The way I see it, although 898 is a tool of the Foundation, it fits the basic criteria for an SCP in that it is a) Supernatural and/or extranormal in character, and b) may be an ongoing issue for the Foundation. It's comparable to SCP-061, in that sense. Plus, it may become an active project again, someday, if the O5's see fit to start it up in the future.

"three (3) years" may seem arbitrary, but that's just because it really is arbitrary. Nevertheless, it's the format that is used throughout the site (I think). Consistency > Reason.

Exposing only one person at a time was something they did in the early stages of testing, but that's no way to get a large body of data. Complicating matters is the fact that not everyone who received SCP-898 treatment responded to it in the same way. In fact, there were some fairly significant differences between subjects. That's part of the reason why the project was abandoned.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
No, I don't think I could. I don't have that good a grasp of neurology myself, and what I've written here was left vague on purpose partly to disguise that lack of knowledge. Besides that, I figure that the more detailed my explanation becomes, the more likely it will be that what I say becomes utter nonsense. Not to mention the fact that it wouldn't be an SCP if there weren't some mystery about how or why it works.

Part of the basis for this SCP idea is that neuroscience is a very young science, and a poorly understood one. There's a lot of stuff about the human brain that still has the character of "black-box" technology, even today. Twenty years ago, it was significantly worse. One of my college professors actually introduced a psychology class with the quote "Everything you learn in here will most likely be proven wrong, or at least somewhat inaccurate, within your lifetime," and based on what I've studied, I'm pretty confident that that statement is true.
